note: Use the app-templates repository as executable architecture. Trace code, deploy one change, break one grant, and explain the boundary.

cards.front: What four contracts should you inspect before reading an app template's business logic?
cards.back: `manifest.yaml` (scaffold inputs), `app.yaml` (runtime command/environment), `databricks.yml` (deployment/resources/targets), and the application entrypoint/routes. AppKit adds `appkit.plugins.json` as the plugin/resource contract.

cards.front: Why is `appkit-all-in-one` a better composition study than starting with a showcase app?
cards.back: It isolates the wiring of analytics, files, Genie, Lakebase, and server plugins. You can see exactly how a capability maps from client route to server plugin to declared resource and privilege before pipeline complexity obscures the boundary.

cards.front: What does an AppKit plugin declaration control?
cards.back: It supplies server-side capability code and names the injected environment/resource contract. The corresponding bundle resource and privilege determine whether the app service principal can actually use the capability.

cards.front: Which AppKit resources does the all-in-one template demonstrate?
cards.back: A SQL warehouse, Unity Catalog Volume, Genie space, and Lakebase Postgres project/branch/database, plus the associated user API scopes and server plugins.

cards.front: Why deliberately remove a resource grant during a template lab?
cards.back: The resulting failure teaches whether the operation depends on app identity, user scope, parent privilege, environment variables, or service availability. Permission failures are architecture evidence, not just bugs.

cards.front: What is the important architectural distinction in `rag-chat`?
cards.back: It is a Lakebase Postgres pgvector implementation with chat history and model/embedding endpoint calls. It is a retrieval pattern and comparison baseline, not the same thing as Databricks AI Search.

cards.front: How should the NFL Media Intelligence Workbench combine templates?
cards.back: Use `appkit-all-in-one` for the shell, files, Lakebase, and Genie; use `e2e-chatbot-app-next` for the chat/agent surface; add a separately benchmarked AI Search layer for governed retrieval. Keep retrieval behind a server interface so the backend can change.

cards.front: Which templates fit a public-document Evidence Assistant?
cards.back: `appkit-files` for Volume browsing, `e2e-chatbot-app-next` for the chat UI, `agent-langgraph` or `agent-openai-agents-sdk` for the agent, and `rag-chat` as a Lakebase pgvector comparison implementation.

cards.front: Which templates fit the NFL Era and Defense-Adjusted QB Lab?
cards.back: Start with `appkit-analytics` and `appkit-genie`; move to `appkit-all-in-one` only when the broader shell is useful. Add model serving only for a real forecast/ranking runtime, not merely because the app is AI-adjacent.

cards.front: What does `e2e-chatbot-app-next` teach that a model-serving demo does not?
cards.back: It shows a complete browser-to-agent application: React/Express structure, Databricks authentication, endpoint permissions, optional Lakebase history, feedback, Bundle targets, and the special grants required for multi-agent endpoints.

cards.front: Why study `agent-langgraph-advanced` after the simpler agent templates?
cards.back: It makes the hidden production concerns explicit: durable checkpointers, long-term memory, background work, streaming, MLflow tracing, request timeouts, and the choice between app identity and user OBO identity.

cards.front: What does the inventory-intelligence Bundle target split demonstrate?
cards.back: An app-only target, a demo target with controlled data, and a full target that adds pipelines/jobs/forecasting. This is a practical way to promote the UI separately from costly or stateful data workloads.

cards.front: What is the special convention in `mcp-server-open-api-spec`?
cards.back: The OpenAPI spec is stored in a Unity Catalog Volume, downstream auth is held in a Unity Catalog HTTP connection, and an app name beginning with `mcp-` supports AI Playground discovery.

cards.front: What must be in a template walkthrough deliverable?
cards.back: One architecture diagram, one request trace, one identity/permission matrix, one deliberate failure transcript, and five recall cards. Source browsing alone does not count as mastery.

cards.front: What is the normal Bundle safety sequence for a dev deployment?
cards.back: `databricks bundle validate -t dev`, then `databricks bundle plan -t dev`, review the plan, and only then run `databricks bundle deploy -t dev`.

cards.front: Why should AppKit API details come from `npx @databricks/appkit docs`?
cards.back: The package and template APIs evolve. Version-local documentation prevents an AI assistant from generating a plausible but stale plugin, hook, or component API.

cards.front: What does a deployed App prove that local `npm run dev` cannot?
cards.back: The deployed service principal, declared-resource grants, user authorization scopes, workspace policies, serverless runtime behavior, injected environment, logs, and the real network path.

cards.front: How should retrieval backend choice be learned rather than assumed?
cards.back: Run the same golden dataset through `rag-chat`/Lakebase pgvector and AI Search, then compare retrieval quality, embedding/chunk choices, filters, freshness, latency, throughput, tuning, governance, portability, operations, and total cost.

cards.front: Why is the app-templates README not sufficient by itself?
cards.back: The README gives the catalog and intended setup, but the architecture is in the resource YAML, plugin manifest, entrypoints, routes, tests, and failure behavior. Read README and code together, then verify product semantics against documentation.

cards.front: What is the first vertical slice for the NFL workbench?
cards.back: Select a public PDF in a Volume, show metadata, answer one citation-bearing question, persist the conversation in Lakebase, and render one Genie/SQL analytics page—using a server abstraction that keeps the retrieval backend replaceable.

cards.front: Which command scaffolds a template from the catalog?
cards.back: `databricks apps init --name <app-name> --template https://github.com/databricks/app-templates/tree/main/<template>`; use the local checkout when you want to inspect or modify the exact source.

cards.front: What is the correct inner loop for a Node/AppKit template?
cards.back: Inspect and modify source in VS Code, run `npm install`, `npm run dev`, and `npm run build`, use local tests/type generation, then deploy a dev App only when resource identity or runtime integration must be proved.

cards.front: What is the correct fourth-day mastery exercise?
cards.back: Close the notes, draw one architecture, explain the request and identity flow, defend one alternative, diagnose a deliberately broken grant, and state what Free Edition still cannot prove about production.
